slides.page_title: Statistics: How the Planner Guesses Row Counts (cont.)

items: `Materialize` caches a subplan so an inner side rescans free
`WindowAgg` runs window functions
`Unique` does DISTINCT over sorted input
`Append` / `Merge Append` for partitions and UNION ALL

blocks.title: Append Family
items: `Append` concatenates children in turn
`Merge Append` merges **sorted** children, keeps order
`Subplans Removed` counts pruned partitions
`WindowAgg` needs input sorted by PARTITION BY, ORDER BY
Expect a `Sort` just below it without an index
A matching index removes that Sort entirely
Compare `rows=` against `actual rows=` at every node
Start from the leaves, walk upward
Error compounds: 10x at a leaf becomes 1000x three joins up
The first big divergence is where the plan broke

blocks.q: Leaf estimates 5 rows, gets 500,000. First move?
a_bullets: ==ANALYZE== the table and re-run the plan
Add extended stats before touching indexes

blocks.title: Leaves First
blocks.text: Fix the lowest node whose estimate is wrong. Everything above it was costed on that bad number.

items: Stale statistics — by far the most common
Check `last_analyze` and `last_autoanalyze`
Both live in `pg_stat_user_tables`
Correlated columns with no extended statistics
Joining on an expression the planner has no stats for
Data skew: one `customer_id` owns 90% of rows
The plan was costed for the average customer
Bloat makes `reltuples` and `relpages` lie about size
`VACUUM FULL` or `pg_repack` resets them

lines: -- replan per call with the real parameter

blocks.title: Flashlight, Not Repair
blocks.text: `enable_nestloop = off` proves which plan you wanted. Then go make the planner want it on its own.

items: `pg_hint_plan` for real hints when nothing else lands
`join_collapse_limit` and `from_collapse_limit` are both 8
Past that many tables the planner stops searching join orders exhaustively

blocks.title: Production Plans
items: `auto_explain` logs plans for slow queries
Catches what you cannot re-run by hand
The plan you reproduce may not be the plan that hurt

caption.text: Part 3 of POSTGRES EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Your query is slow and the plan is 40 lines of indented noise — here is how to read it in three moves. Ten pages on every scan and join node, where cost numbers actually come from, how the planner guesses row counts, and the exact signatures that tell you it guessed wrong. Save it for the next 2am incident.
